Nodes.Speaker: ronin
Nodes.Text: Keep walking. I owe nobody a sword -- least of all a caravan that wakes the ground wherever it steps.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: You're bleeding into the grass. Let us patch you up, and stand with us while we clear this field.

Nodes.Speaker: ronin
Nodes.Text: ...You mended a stranger and fought beside him without asking his name. Fine. My blade walks with yours.

Nodes.Speaker: merc
Nodes.Text: Sand in my boots, no coin in my purse. A hundred and fifty gold and I'm yours till the dunes stop moving.

Nodes.Speaker: merc
Nodes.Text: Coin's counted. Point me at whatever's crawling out of the sand.

Nodes.Speaker: freed
Nodes.Text: They had me chained where the ground had already started to sour. Another day and I'd have been grown into the stones. You came through all of that -- for a stranger?

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Nobody gets left standing still out here. The Longmother keeps walking, and so do we.

Nodes.Speaker: freed
Nodes.Text: Then I owe you my legs, at the very least. Where does this caravan need them?

Choices.Label: Walk with us. There's a place in the line for you.
Rest first. The road will still be here.

Nodes.Speaker: freed
Nodes.Text: Rest is for ground that isn't waking. I'll sleep in the wagon -- and fight beside you when it stops.

Nodes.Speaker: freed
Nodes.Text: Count me in. Whatever held me will learn what it let go of.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Hold up there -- you're the ones who dropped at the last footfall, aren't you? I heard you cleared it before the ground even finished shaking.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Word travels faster than we do, apparently. What do you need?

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Not a thing -- I'm offering. I've been riding a few wagons back of every crew since the wells turned, and a caravan this size could use another set of wheels. Let me ride with you?

Choices.Label: Welcome aboard.
First, sell us a map. (20 G)
We travel alone.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Smart. Here -- the roads past the valley, marked true, and a tonic for the nerves. On the house, since you're paying for the ink.

Choices.Label: Then ride with us.
Safe travels.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Suit yourselves. I'll follow a few wagons back all the same -- somebody has to sell you rope when you run out.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Good. Find my wagon at camp whenever you need supplies -- and don't let that caravan guard talk you into anything expensive.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: So this is really how it works -- we drop, we clear, we grab what's useful, and she just... keeps walking.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: That's the whole trade, far as I've ever seen it. Stand still too long anywhere on this road and you'll learn why she doesn't.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: You're the crew that cleared the slime nest? I watched from the ridge -- didn't think three of you would still be standing.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: We nearly weren't. We could use another pair of hands, if you're offering.

Choices.Label: Join us.
The road is dangerous.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Dangerous is why I'm still out here instead of back where the wells turned. I can handle it.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Then that's settled. Where this caravan's headed, it'll want someone who can still cast a straight line.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: That's the road clear behind us, for now. Feels like the first time any of us has stopped moving in days.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: You look it. I've got a wagon with real beds, not bedrolls on a cart floor -- first good sleep since the wells turned sour, if you'll have it.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Shall I hitch my wagon to yours, then?

Choices.Label: Please do.
We can't pay much.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: A fair price for people who clear footfalls for a living. I wasn't going to charge you much anyway.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Good. Rest at camp whenever the road wears you down -- the Longmother doesn't stop, but you're allowed to.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: That gear of yours is chewed half through. Whatever you've been fighting, it's eating your steel faster than you can swing it.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Faster than we'd like. Can it be mended?

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Mended, reforged, melted down for something better -- whatever it needs. Take me along and you'll never fight on a notched blade again. Well?

Choices.Label: Bring your anvil.
Prove it first.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Fair. Bring the worst of it to my forge-cart at camp and watch -- it'll come back whole before your stew's cold.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Good. Find me at the forge-cart before something breaks -- once it shatters, there's nothing left to mend.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Travelers -- thank every working gear in creation. The sand took my cart two days back and the goblin digs further in are not polite company.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Ride with the caravan, then. We're headed through the Reaches ourselves.

Choices.Label: Join us.
The road is dangerous.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: I've rebuilt worse than danger out of spare parts. Danger I can work with.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Then my tools are yours. Fair warning -- I fix things that are already broken a lot better than I avoid breaking them in the first place.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Hold on -- what's that hanging off your packs? Pelts, wings, glands... Most crews sell those to the Merchant for coppers. Bottled right, they close a wound.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: What are you brewing all the way out here?

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Whatever your crews pull off the things you kill. Venom, ichor, pelt -- it's all reagent if you know how to read it, and a potion brewed costs a fraction of one bought. Need a brewer?

Choices.Label: Join us.
Is it safe?

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Mostly. I'm coming either way -- the road's not safe for a brewer working alone, and lately neither is a clean spell.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Good. Here -- a clean bottle for your first brew. Find me at camp with those trophies; the Merchant sells more bottles for a few coins.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: The works under these dunes aren't the Longmother's leavings -- those digs are older than her whole stride through here.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Older than her stride, maybe. Not older than whatever's souring the ground. That didn't start with us, and it isn't finishing with us either.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Who goes there, in the Frostmaw dark? Answer slow -- I've had worse than bandits down this pass.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Friends, if you'll have us. We're with the caravan on the Longmother's back.

Choices.Label: Join us.
The road is dangerous.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: I've held this pass alone a full season. Danger and I are well acquainted.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Then my shield walks with you. Whatever's down here that's built and not grown, I want to see it fall as much as you do.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: That thing we pulled out of the ice wasn't grown. It was built. On purpose.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: I've forged enough to know the difference between an accident and a design. That was a design. Somebody made that, somewhere, a long time before we ever got here.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Hold still -- you're bleeding from that last stretch of ruin and you don't even seem to know it.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Mend us, and march with us. We won't say no to either.

Choices.Label: Join us.
The road is dangerous.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: The ruins are worse than anything on the road behind you. I'd rather face them with company.

Nodes.Speaker: recruit
Nodes.Text: Then I'll keep you standing. Whatever's waiting in here that refuses to lie down, we're going to make sure it finally does.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: A dead city that tried to just... stay. No Longmother, no walking, just walls.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: And it still didn't work. Whatever's waiting in there has had longer than anyone to learn what staying still actually costs.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: The Vampire Lord's down, and we're back in green country. I almost thought that was the end of it.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: It never was going to be. She can't walk back over ground she's already woken, so she curls instead -- and we end up somewhere that looks like home and isn't. Deeper in than the old road ever ran.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: This isn't rare anymore. Half of what we're fighting out here is half-built like that thing near the ridge.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Out past the Reaches, it's the norm, not the exception. We give the strong ones a single name, like it's one throne and not a condition. I don't think it's one throne.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Those markings on the wreck back there -- that's not our caravan's make.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: No. Somebody else was working this ground before us, and didn't get the chance to leave. Past the mire, nobody comes this far who still has somewhere better to be.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: The ore's thinner down here. Half of what we're hauling up doesn't burn clean anymore.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Then we stop trusting it to burn clean and start trusting it less. Whatever's down at the bottom of these veins isn't interested in making this easy for us.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: We're past where the Vampire Lord held, and the ruins just... keep going. Older under older.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Then the road's not done asking its question. We've beaten what was standing in the doorway. We still don't know what built the house.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: You followed my lights a long way to show me fresh armor. Honest work -- but it's only leather and stitching. It could be more.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: More how? Who are you?

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: One who binds workings into what you wear instead of trusting them to the air. A rune in a jerkin can knit wounds, keep out venom, or bite back at whatever strikes it. Your caravan could use that.

Choices.Label: Then come with us.
Show us a rune.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: Fair enough -- there. Bound tight enough to last a march; most spells aren't, anymore.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: Good. Take this pinch of Arcane Dust -- bring it to my table with a few trophies from the road, and I'll bind your first rune into that armor for nothing.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Every fen's worse than the last fen. That's not a feeling anymore, that's just the route.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: Because the blight pools where the ground's low and wet, same as anything else that doesn't like to keep moving. We're walking into exactly what it likes best.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Welcome back. Wares, news, or just killing time before the next footfall?

Choices.Label: About that map...
Sorry we turned you away.
Can your guard join us? (300 G)
Just passing by.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: That map's good as far as the Reaches -- past that, you're trusting the same ruts I am.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Already forgotten. A crew that turns away a stranger on a bad road isn't wrong to, most days.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Good man. Treat my guard well -- he's saved my hide more than the map ever has.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Safe roads. Mind the wells.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Beds are made, water's hot. What's keeping you up?

Choices.Label: Any news from the road?
Goodnight.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Travelers talk more than they think when they're warm and fed. I just listen -- you'd be surprised what a crew says the night after a bad footfall.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Sleep while you can. The ground doesn't wait for anyone, but you've earned the night.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Mind the sparks. What do you need -- mended, or melted down?

Choices.Label: Where did you learn the trade?
Carry on.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: My mother's forge, a long time before the wells turned. She worked shed-plate same as I do now. Guess some trades just keep walking.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Bring me something broken. There's always something broken.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Don't touch the green one. What do you need?

Choices.Label: What does the green one do?
I'll leave you to it.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Not entirely sure yet. That's half the reason it's still in the flask and not in somebody's potion belt.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Bring me reagents. The good kind come off the things that still twitch after you've killed them.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: The runes are restless tonight. What do you need?

Choices.Label: Restless how?
Goodnight.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: They hum, faint, when something's close that magic doesn't like the shape of. Out here, that's most nights.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: Sleep lightly. I'll be listening to the steel.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Didn't expect to be out here when the season started, if I'm honest. Strange how fast normal changes.

Choices.Label: How are you holding up?
What do you make of the merchant?
Rest well.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Tired. Everyone's tired. But we're still standing, and that counts for something out here.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: He talks too much and prices everything, but he hasn't steered us wrong yet. I'll take it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: You too. Try to actually sleep -- the ground'll still be there in the morning. Probably.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Same fight again today. I held the line. Didn't move a tile. That's a win, isn't it?

Choices.Label: Holding still isn't winning. Keep one hit on your bar and use it.
Exactly. A wall that never moves never loses.
Move less, even. Let them wear themselves out on you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Huh. A wall with a door in it. I can hold that thought. Same as everything else.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Yeah. That's what I keep telling myself. Same thing every fight.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I swore an oath long before this caravan. Lately I can't remember to whom. Does it still bind me?

Choices.Label: Then it's void. Swear a new one to the Longmother.
An oath kept for no one in particular is still kept. Keeping it is the point.
Forget oaths. Just fight for yourself.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Kept, then, and that is the point. ...I believe that was meant to be the joke. It landed late. As usual.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Perhaps. It does not sit right, though. I shall keep thinking on it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: The Barbarian out-hit me again. Should I trade my potion slot for another attack? Everyone's hurt anyway.

Choices.Label: Yes -- matching the Barbarian's damage is how you earn your place.
Drop the potion and let the Cleric carry you.
Keep the potion. You don't need to out-damage anyone; you just need to never run out.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Right. The potion stays. Now -- let me see that cut. You first, then me.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Maybe. Hold still, you're bleeding. We'll argue about my bar later.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Left. Right. Hold. ...There's no line beside me. I keep counting cadence for a formation that isn't there.

Choices.Label: A formation of one is still a formation -- hold it as discipline, not as missing someone.
Wait for the others to catch up before you fight at all.
Stop counting. Formations are for armies, not caravans.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Formation of one. Hold. ...Steady. That I can do.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Negative. Without the cadence I'm just a man standing in a field.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Tank. I'm the Tank. That's all there is to me, right? Nothing to learn when you're the obvious pick.

Choices.Label: Right. You're simple, and that's all you need to be.
Obvious doesn't mean finished. There's plenty left to learn about yourself.
Pick a fancier class. Nobody remembers the obvious one.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Plenty left to learn. Huh. ...Tank, still learning. I'll put that on the shield.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Okay. Tank. Glad that's settled.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I marked our target for us -- for all of us! So why are we hitting three different things?

Choices.Label: Mark it louder. They'll follow eventually.
Stop marking things. Let everyone pick their own fight.
Marking the target isn't the same as us following you there. Bring them with you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Bring them with us. Yes. We mark it together, then we go together. That's ours to fix.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Louder, then! We'll get there. All of us. Eventually.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Planted my banner at the first fight of the season. Long time back, now. The banner's still there. Still counts, eh?

Choices.Label: A banner only means something while someone's standing under it. Keep renewing it.
It counts forever. You earned your rest.
Banners are old ways. Let the young ones lead.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Renew it. Hm. That's a thing my old chief said, once. Took me forty years to hear it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Maybe. When I was your age, we didn't ask whether banners counted.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: The caravan doesn't ask how I keep them safe. Only that I do. That should settle it, shouldn't it?

Choices.Label: If nobody's judging, there's nothing to worry about.
Them not judging the method doesn't make it free. Count the cost yourself.
Go back to a Knight's methods. Leave the dark rites alone.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Count it myself. Yes. Someone ought to, and it should be the one paying.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Then it's settled. It doesn't feel settled. But fine.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Sorry -- I know draining them works, I just -- it feels wrong every time. Am I doing it badly? Sorry.

Choices.Label: If it feels wrong, it probably is. Stop draining.
Get used to it. Feelings slow you down.
Being uncomfortable with a tactic isn't the same as doing it wrong.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Uncomfortable, not wrong. Oh. That's -- thank you. Sorry. I mean, thank you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Ah. Right. Sorry. I'll... try that, I suppose.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: My output is forty percent below the Red Mage's. Should I convert my reagents into offense to close the gap?

Choices.Label: Out-damaging the mages was never your job. Never running out is the brag.
Yes, damage is the only number anyone reads.
Hoard the reagents for the boss and do nothing until then.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Never running out. Correct. The sum checks. I'll stop measuring myself against the wrong column.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Hm. My math disagrees, but I'll note your figure.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: That beast was one hit from falling. I nearly stepped up to finish it myself. Would that have been wrong?

Choices.Label: No -- a kill is a kill. Take it when you can.
Yes. Chasing a kill on the front line is the one way to lose the sustain war.
Only if your bar has nothing better. Otherwise go for it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Then I'll stay back, and keep them alive when they shouldn't be. That is the job.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Perhaps. I'll consider it. Calmly.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I treated the worst wound first. The one I treated last hasn't spoken to me since. Was I wrong?

Choices.Label: You should treat friends first. That's loyalty.
Treat whoever complains loudest. Keeps the peace.
You triaged right. Done right, triage still looks cold to whoever's last.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Right is still cold. Yes. I'll go explain it to them. After I check who's bleeding.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Noted. Now -- who's bleeding worse? Not you. Next.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I saw the mirror-curse coming three turns out. As I expected, it landed. Why does nobody thank me?

Choices.Label: Being right isn't the same as warning anyone in time to use it.
They're jealous of your foresight. Ignore them.
Stop predicting. It only makes you miserable.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Warned in time. Yes. Knowing alone was never the gift. As I should have expected.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: As I expected. ...Which is the trouble, isn't it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: My ward was so lovely after the hit landed -- everyone was healed in one glow. Isn't that the point?

Choices.Label: Yes. A pretty ward after the fact is still a ward.
A ward is for before the hit. Cast it early, don't admire it after.
Skip wards. Heal one at a time.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Before, not after. How rude of me to keep them waiting. Thank you, dear.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: How kind of you. I'm sure it will all work out, somehow.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Where does peace live, I wonder? I hand it to the party, and it's gone before they sit down.

Choices.Label: Peace lives in the heart. Keep wandering.
Stop handing it out. Peace is a private thing.
Peace has to be somewhere they can stand -- put it on the ground, not just in the feeling.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Peace you can stand on. ...That is a better question than mine. Thank you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Is the heart where you stand, though? We'll see.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I blessed us all before we left the town. That should hold us the whole way, as the old saying goes.

Choices.Label: One blessing doesn't cover the expedition. It's a line item, not a shield.
It does. A blessing given in faith never runs out.
Bless only yourself. You matter most.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A line item -- my, how practical. Then I'll bless us again before every fight.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Ah, 'the old saying goes.' Wherever it goes. I'm sure it holds.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I reached three allies in one turn. Fast. ...One of them was the one who was dying, wasn't it.

Choices.Label: Three is more than one. Speed is everything.
Speed covers a lot, but not for skipping the one who's actually dying.
Slow down entirely. Speed is a trap.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Dying first. Speed second. Understood.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Fast. Yes.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: The weather says a bad fight tomorrow. I told everyone. Done. Warning discharged.

Choices.Label: Then your part's done. Let them deal with it.
Keep omens to yourself. They just scare people.
Saying the omen out loud doesn't discharge it. We still have to act on it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Act on it. ...Very well. I'll ask what we're doing about it. That part's actually reassuring.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Done, then. It will rain, regardless.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Blade, then fire, then blade -- I'm good at both, so why not be best at both? Just need more practice!

Choices.Label: Chasing best-at-both is how you end up merely good at both. Pick what the fight needs.
Exactly. Practice both twice as hard.
Drop the blade. Mages shouldn't touch steel.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Pick what it needs. Huh. That's -- okay, that's one thing at a time. I can try one thing at a time.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Twice as hard! On it -- right after this cast and this swing and--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I'll stay with this caravan for now. Just for now. I haven't committed to anything.

Choices.Label: Good. Keep your options open.
You've been here long enough that staying already is the commitment.
Then leave. Nobody needs a maybe.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Already committed. Huh. I suppose I have been. For now. -- No. Just: I have been.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: For now, then.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Debrief: four enemies down, one ally hurt, objective met. Do you want the written report as well?

Choices.Label: Yes. File it with the Merchant.
Make the reports longer. More detail.
We don't need a report. We need a teammate.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Copy. No report. Teammate. Adjusting. -- That was a joke. Mostly.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Report filed. Moving on.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...The party goes quiet when I walk past. Good. Quiet is efficient.

Choices.Label: A party that's a bit scared of you won't tell you when something's wrong.
Good. Fear keeps them in line.
Then stay out of their way entirely.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Then I'll be less frightening. Slightly. Don't tell anyone I said that.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Efficient.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Seven ticks of the working, seven measures of pain. It is a rite, not cruelty.

Choices.Label: Right. A rite is holy; holy things cost nothing.
Calling it a rite doesn't make the cost to the target any less real.
Stop the rites. Use plain spells.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: The cost remains. The rite does not wash it. ...Let it be counted honestly, then.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: So it is written. So it is done.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: One, two, three, FIGHT! I'll smash the front rank eventually, right? Warm-up turns are fine!

Choices.Label: Sure. Take your time and build up to it.
Hang back and let the Paladin go first.
'I delete the front rank' has to be true on turn one, not eventually.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Turn one! Okay, okay -- three, two, one, SMASH. Got it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Eventually it is! Warm-ups are the fun part.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Hit. Simple. People think simple means dumb.

Choices.Label: Simple and thoughtless aren't the same word, and you've earned the difference.
Simple is dumb. Learn some fancy moves.
Don't worry about what people think. Just hit.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Earned. Good.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Swung for the knockout and missed, ha! Lost again! Next time it'll land, right?

Choices.Label: Ha! Keep swinging. Luck evens out.
A haymaker that misses costs the same turn as one that lands. Recklessness has a clock too.
Never swing big. Only jab.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Same turn either way. Huh. ...That's a lot of turns I've spent. Okay. I'll pick my moments.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: That's the spirit! Next one lands for sure! Probably!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Hehe, they always think I'm harmless right up until the Slam! That works on everybody, right?

Choices.Label: Yep! Keep the cute act forever.
Drop the cute act. Be scary all the time.
Being underestimated works once per stranger. The party already knows -- we need something else from you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Something else, for you all... okay! Less surprise, more teamwork. Then the Slam.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Hehe! Everybody. Always. ...Right?

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Buy heavier armor. Survive longer. Yes?

Choices.Label: No. Gearing for survival is gearing away from the point. Hit and harvest.
Yes. Survival comes first.
Become a tank for a while.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Hit. Harvest. Light.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Heavier, then.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: My opponent stumbled. I waited for them to recover their guard. It seemed only proper.

Choices.Label: Of course. Honor matters more than winning.
Respecting an opponent isn't the same as waiting for them to be ready.
Never respect an enemy. They're monsters.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A fair point, fairly made. I shall respect them -- and strike while they stumble.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Quite. One must observe the forms.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Lunge, lunge, and -- nobody was ready for my lunge, which is their problem, not mine, right? Right.

Choices.Label: Right. Lunge first, explain never.
Learn to retreat. Lunging is reckless.
A lunge that can't reverse is something the party has to plan around. Tell them first.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Tell them first -- yes, so they can, exactly, plan for -- got it. Telling them.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Right, their problem, exactly what I was--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: You give orders. I consider them. Sometimes I follow. I chose this caravan, after all.

Choices.Label: Choosing to stay means choosing to take direction sometimes, or the choice stops meaning anything.
Exactly. Masterless means you owe no one.
Then leave, if orders bother you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Then I will take direction. Sometimes more than sometimes. I'll consider it seriously.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A suggestion worth considering. I will consider it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: My contract with the merchant ran out ages ago. Should I renegotiate? I don't work for free.

Choices.Label: Yes -- ask for double. You're worth it.
The contract ended and you stayed anyway. That's a choice, not a line item -- say it out loud.
Quit. No pay, no work.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Not a line item. ...Fine. I'm staying because I want to. Don't put that in the ledger.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Double, then. I'll draw up the papers.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: The battle was lost, but the final cut was perfect. Truly, the form was flawless.

Choices.Label: The form is all that matters. Bless the blade.
Forget form entirely. Swing wildly.
A perfect cut on a lost fight is still a loss. We need the win more than the form.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: The win over the form. ...Then the form must serve the win. That is a deeper discipline.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Flawless. As it should be.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Got a ring, two coins, a weird spoon -- from every fight! The party should be thrilled, right? Anyway--

Choices.Label: Grabbing loot every fight isn't the same as having something to show the party for it.
Absolutely. Keep picking pockets.
Give up stealing. It's beneath you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Something to show them... okay, the spoon goes in the camp pot. Contributions!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Thrilled! Ooh, what's in your bag?

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...The others are variations on me. I'm the plain one.

Choices.Label: Right. Plain is all you are.
Being the template doesn't mean you have nothing of your own to say. Just say it shorter.
Change colors. Be different.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Shorter. Mine.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I remain calm under pressure. Why does the party think I'm absent?

Choices.Label: They're just jealous of your composure.
Panic a little more. It's relatable.
Calm that reads as distance is still distance. Let them see that you care.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Visible, then. Acceptable. I'll try to look as present as I am.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Obviously.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Red one fight, blue the next, green after -- I'm wonderfully flexible! Why don't they rely on me?

Choices.Label: Flexibility without a throughline reads as unreliable. Give them one thing they can count on.
Be even more unpredictable!
Pick one color forever and never change.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: One thing to count on... the throughline. Every color, still me. I like that.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Even more! Watch -- purple!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Ta-da! Teleported right behind it! ...It wasn't really in a better spot, but did you see that?

Choices.Label: Flashy counts! Keep the show going.
A sooner position has to mean something tactically, not just look flashy.
Never teleport. Walk like everybody else.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Something tactically -- ugh, fine. A trick with a point. That's the harder trick.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Ha! See? Flashy counts!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Reached their backline before the Assassin again. That's two-to-one. Not that I'm counting.

Choices.Label: Keep beating the Assassin. That's what matters.
Copy the Assassin exactly. It works for them.
Find what you do that the Assassin doesn't. Racing to the backline isn't a personality.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: What I do that they don't... Flamefang. The fire. Fine. That's mine.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Two-to-one. Not counting. Three soon.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: There was an opening -- so I went -- immediately -- and it was a trap -- but it WAS an opening!

Choices.Label: Not every opening needs taking the instant it appears. Some are worth waiting a turn on.
Faster is always better! Go go go!
Never take openings. They're all traps.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Wait one turn. One. One whole turn. ...Okay. Okay okay. I can do one.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Go go go! Yes! Exactly what I--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I announce my charge, and then I charge. A courtesy. After the charge, I... think about it later.

Choices.Label: Charge harder and the after takes care of itself.
Telegraphing is fine, but only if there's still a plan for after it lands.
Stop announcing it. Surprise is everything.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A plan for after. Then I shall announce that, too. Courteously.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Harder, then. Understood. Charging.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Bag's heavy! Fight was rough -- we barely made it -- but look at all this! Next stage?

Choices.Label: Heavy bag means a good day. Next stage!
Leave the loot behind entirely.
Plunder from a fight we barely survived isn't a win just because the bag's heavier.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Barely survived... right. Fewer grabs, more of us walking out. Bag's still heavy, though.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Exactly! Next stage!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Whyisthiscampsoslow? I'm faster than everyone. Speed is the plan. The whole plan.

Choices.Label: Speed isn't a plan. It's a resource, and it runs out just like mana.
Yes! Just keep going faster.
Slow down to everyone else's pace.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A resource. Spend it, don't burn it. Okay -- slower thought, faster feet.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Faster! Already ahead of you!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Pocket sand worked great last week, heh. Using it again tomorrow on the same pack.

Choices.Label: Never change a winning move.
A trick that works once stops being a trick the second time an enemy remembers it.
Fight fair, like the Duelist.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Heh. Fair -- they'll remember. Guess I need a new pocket.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Exactly, champ. Never change.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: That fight ran two turns long, and I didn't land the finishing blow. Unacceptable.

Choices.Label: Agreed. Finishes are your whole job.
Stop finishing things. Let it run long.
Not every fight is owed a finish from you. It belongs to whoever has the opening.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Whoever has the opening. ...Fine. Faster that way, anyway.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Next time. On schedule.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: One, two, three -- the chain broke at three. So I started over at one. Like I was taught.

Choices.Label: A chain broken early isn't a restart cue. It's a signal to change the plan for that fight.
Yes. Always restart the chain.
Stop chaining entirely.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Change the plan. ...Nobody taught me that part. Thank you.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: One, two, three. One, two, three.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Note how my palm strike transfers force through the hips! I explained it to the party mid-fight -- with diagrams!

Choices.Label: More diagrams. Teaching never stops.
The lesson can wait until the enemy's down. Narrating mid-fight is a liability.
Stop teaching altogether.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A good lesson for the teacher. Fight first, lecture after. Note it down.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Indeed! Now observe the footwork--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Did you see that knockout? The crowd -- I mean the party -- loved it! Gotta give 'em a show!

Choices.Label: Yes! Bigger show next time!
Stop fighting flashy. Hide in the back.
The party isn't an audience. Coordinate with them, don't play to them.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Not an audience. A corner team. ...I can work with a corner team.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Bigger! Ladies and gentlemen--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Jab. Cross. Done. They say I don't care. I care about the next hit.

Choices.Label: Economy of motion doesn't need economy of warmth. Let them see you're with them.
Good. Keep quiet. Focus.
Throw bigger punches.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Fair. I'll say 'good hit' more. When it is one.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I tracked it across the whole field. The opening never came. I'll keep waiting.

Choices.Label: Patience always pays. Keep waiting.
Sometimes we can't afford the wait. Make the opening instead of finding it.
Stop tracking. Just charge.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Make it. ...The prey would never expect that. Neither would I.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Then I wait.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Heh. I'm always right there when they're hurt. Collecting. The party gives me looks for it.

Choices.Label: Keep circling. Who cares about their looks.
Hit first for once. Take the hard part.
Collecting only works if the party trusts you're collecting, not just circling. Tell them.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Tell them. Heh. Fine -- I'll call my collections.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Heh. Circling.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...One draw. One cut. Then I rest.

Choices.Label: The perfect draw is still only one action. The fight goes on after your turn.
Yes. One cut is enough.
Draw twice. Always twice.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Then the next breath, too.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Twelve cuts! Thirteen! Fourteen! That's a lot of cuts, that guard's gotta be broken, right? Right?!

Choices.Label: Yes! More cuts means more broken.
Count of hits isn't the same as the guard actually being broken. Check the result.
Use one big cut instead.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Check the result. ...Fourteen cuts and -- oh, it's still standing. Good catch.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Fifteen! Sixteen!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I have endured past what should have ended me. Is that survival... or only a longer refusal to stop?

Choices.Label: It's just survival. Don't think about it.
You should have stopped. Stop now.
That's your question to answer -- but enduring for the caravan, not away from it, is a reason, not a refusal.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A reason, and not a refusal. ...I have not been offered that before. I'll keep it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Perhaps. Time will tell. Time always does, for me.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I roared and every foe came for me! Glorious! ...Then I fell over. But glorious!

Choices.Label: A roar that draws attention has to be backed by surviving the attention it draws.
Roar louder next time!
Never roar. Hide.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Survive the attention... then I'll eat my potion before the roar. Still glorious.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: LOUDER! Yes!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Pack knows. I move, pack follows. Don't need words.

Choices.Label: Right. Words are useless.
The pack includes people who need the plan said out loud, not just felt.
Talk constantly so no one is confused.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Said out loud. Okay. 'Left.' Like that?

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Yes. No words.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: A wolf that fights beside us today could bite us tomorrow. How do I keep it with us?

Choices.Label: Chain it up and drag it along.
Fight beside it until it trusts you. A full bond keeps it for good.
Keep it hungry so it stays loyal.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Trust first, then the pack. I'll stay close and let it watch me fight.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: That breaks a beast. It doesn't bond one.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I passed the warning to everyone -- left flank, two turns -- and then I was off to the next thing! Message delivered!

Choices.Label: Delivered is done. Next message!
Stop relaying. People should find out themselves.
Relaying it isn't the same as making sure someone actually acted on it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Acted on, not just heard -- I'll circle back! One loop, quick!

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Delivered! Next--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Round and round I go, and somewhere in the spin it all lands, doesn't it? You'll trust it lands?

Choices.Label: We need to catch you mid-spin before we can trust where it's going. Tell us where.
Spin faster -- it'll land somewhere good.
Stop spinning. Stand still.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Tell you where... a spin with a destination. That's still a spin. I'll aim it.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Faster, faster, round and--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Overclocked the mine, the turret, and myself -- third expedition running. Tolerance is fine. Probably.

Choices.Label: Push harder. Limits are suggestions.
Overclocking a mine is a trick. Overclocking yourself every trip is burnout with better branding.
Stop building devices.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...Rated capacity. For me too. Fine. Running at spec tonight.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Pushing to one-twenty, then.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: My turret's still running from last fight. Beautiful machine. I'll build a second one beside it.

Choices.Label: Two turrets is twice as good.
Sell the turret.
Know when to stop building and fight directly. A turret past its fight is scrap waiting to jam.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Stop building, start fighting. ...Then the turret earns its rest, and so do I.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Two it is. Hand me the wrench.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Probability of success, sixty-two percent. Running the diagnostic again to refine that. Out loud.

Choices.Label: A diagnostic out loud mid-fight costs time we may not have. Sometimes guess at speed.
Refine it to ninety-nine before acting.
Never calculate anything.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Guess at speed. ...Estimated confidence: higher than before. Fine.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Refining. Sixty-two point four...

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Patched the gear with tape and wire, works fine now, see? Oh -- that strap's loose, hold on--

Choices.Label: Works is works. Move on to the next fix.
'It works' isn't the same as 'it'll keep working.' Patch it to last.
Throw it away and buy new.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Patch it to last. Right, the shatter. ...Two more wraps of tape. Three, actually.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Works! Next one-- where's my--

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: I took the shot. Got paid. Why does the rest of you want an explanation?

Choices.Label: You don't owe them anything. Paid is paid.
Stop taking shots for coin.
Being paid doesn't mean the shot owes the party no explanation. Mercenary isn't the same as silent.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: ...An explanation. Fine. Billed as a courtesy.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Paid is paid.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: This fen is mine to guard. You trample it, you get a snare. Why should I stand down?

Choices.Label: We're crossing the fen out of need, not malice. Your suspicion can stand down for that.
Never stand down. Snare everyone.
Leave the fen behind. It's just mud.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Need, not malice... fine. The fen will let you pass. This once. Mind the reeds.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Snare everyone. Good. The fen agrees.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Shoot, fall back, shoot again. Never where I fired from. Never where they can reach me. Never anywhere, really.

Choices.Label: Good. Keep running, from everyone.
Keeping your distance from foes is the job. You don't have to keep it from us.
Stop falling back. Plant your feet and trade hits.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: From foes, not from you lot. ...I'll drift a little closer to the fire tonight.

Nodes.Speaker: hero
Nodes.Text: Never anywhere. That's safest.

Title: What We Swore For
Crawl:
Somewhere between one footfall and the next, the crew stopped being the new faces on the chain.

The rail-hands nod now when you come back up. The cooks save the good end of the pot. Children on the upper streets have started playing at being you -- dropping off crates onto the cobbles, shouting the pincer call, arguing over who gets to be the one who falls and gets back up.

It would be easy to keep going on that alone. Most crews do, right up until the season they don't come back.

But the road has been saying something, footfall after footfall, and it gets louder the further she walks. The things that come up out of the ground are older here, and stranger, and some of them were built. Someone, a long time ago, wanted this blight to be what it is. Someone is still out there who wants the Longmother to stop.

That changes what the oath is for. A vanguard crew clears a step. What you are turning into might have to clear the road.

So that night, around a fire on the Longmother's back, with the whole town swaying gently under the stars, somebody finally asks the question every crew avoids.

Why are you really here?

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Ten levels of scar tissue and you still eat like you're expecting the bell. Sit. The pot can wait. I want to ask you something I ask every crew that makes it this far.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Every crew that makes it this far. How many is that?

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Four, in my time. Two of them couldn't answer, and they didn't make it much further. So. When you put your hand on her plate and swore -- what were you swearing for?

Choices.Label: For the coin. Somebody has to get paid for this.
For the people below. Someone has to stand where she lands.
To find out who made the blight, and make them answer for it.
Honestly? For the crew. These are my people now.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Ha. Honest, at least. Coin keeps a crew fed, and fed crews come back. Just remember that whoever's waiting at the end of this road won't be paying.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: The town says that one at the rail and forgets it by supper. You didn't forget. Keep it close -- it's the kind of reason that holds when the others snap.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Careful. Every crew that went looking for whoever's behind the blight found something first. But if anyone's going to put a name to it, I'd rather it was you.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: That's the one the four had in common. Not the coin, not the cause. Each other. You'll want that, where she's taking us.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Then we keep walking. Wherever she goes, we drop first -- and we come back up the chain together.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: The new chain crew. I wondered when she'd send somebody down after the last lot. Fine work on their gear, by the way. It fits my soldiers nicely.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: You took it off the crew that didn't come back. You're squatting on a footfall -- the blight will have you by spring.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: Maybe. But this field is mine until it does, and in my field the rules you learned at the rail don't hold. Come and find out which ones.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Everyone, eyes open. Whatever he's got, we learn it fast and we flank it anyway.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: MOTION DETECTED. MOTION IS NOT PERMITTED. THIS SECTOR HOLDS. THIS SECTOR HAS ALWAYS HELD.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: It's been standing here longer than the dunes. The blight never touched it -- it doesn't care, and it doesn't rot.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: INTRUDERS WILL CONFORM TO SECTOR PROTOCOL. STANDARD ENGAGEMENT RULES: SUSPENDED.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Suspended. Wonderful. Watch how it moves before you commit -- machines have patterns.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: Oh, little walkers. You come down into my fen thinking the ground is the danger. The ground is my oldest friend. We came to an arrangement, it and I.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: You let the blight in on purpose. Half the hags in this marsh are wearing it.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: I let it teach me. And what it taught me is that the way you fight -- all those tidy lines and flanks -- is only a habit. Habits break.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Then we'll break hers first. Stay close, keep each other standing.

Title: The Old One Under the Ice

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: ...Small. Quick. Loud. I have slept since before your spider learned to walk, and now you come stamping in my halls.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: The cold kept you. Kept the blight slow in you, too. Whatever you were, you're carrying it now.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: Time is a long teacher. I learned the shape of every fight that ever came down here. Yours too. The old ways do not work on me.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Then we'll find a new one. Spread out, keep moving, and don't give it a target it expects.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: So this is what she sends. Children on chains. Do you know how tired she is? Do you ever listen to her, between the footfalls?

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: We know what you want. You want her to stop, here, on your dead stone, so you can finally rest with company.

Nodes.Speaker: boss
Nodes.Text: I want the walking to end. I made stillness last past death; I can make it last past her. And in my city, little vanguard, I decide how a battle is fought.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: This is the knot in the road. Everything we've learned comes down to this footfall. Together -- now!

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Water carriers came back with half their barrels and all their nerves gone. Wolves have learned the path to the last sweet well. Five fewer wolves and they'd find somewhere else to learn things.

Choices.Label: We'll thin the pack.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Bless you. I'll keep something warm on the shelf for when you're back.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Fair. It'll keep -- the wolves certainly will. It's in your journal if you change your mind.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Here's a theory nobody's paying me for yet: the frogs carry the well-taint before the water does. Three glands and I'll know. Then somebody pays me for it.

Choices.Label: We'll bring you three.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: Fresh ones, if you can. Well -- as fresh as anything off a frog gets.

Nodes.Speaker: merchant
Nodes.Text: The offer stands. Theories don't spoil. Glands do, but that's a later problem.

Nodes.Speaker: with
Nodes.Text: Something I keep thinking about: the blight only catches what holds still. A small crew moves faster. I'd like to prove it -- the next valley, three of us, no more.

Choices.Label: Let's prove it.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: with
Nodes.Text: Green Valley III, three in the fight. Pick them well -- the rest can cheer from the wagons.

Nodes.Speaker: with
Nodes.Text: Fine by me. I'll put it in the journal and keep thinking out loud.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: The gremlins out here carry cogs with teeth no file ever cut. I've worked metal my whole life and I can't say how they were made. Bring me four and I'll find out.

Choices.Label: Four cogs, coming up.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Good. Don't clean them. I want to see the grain.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Suit yourself. It'll gnaw at me, but I've had worse company.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Couldn't sleep. Those cogs -- the blight isn't copying us. It's doing what a forge does, the slow way, with whatever stands still long enough.

Nodes.Speaker: lead
Nodes.Text: Then the longer something stays put, the more it gets... made into something.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Right. Which means a working forge on a walking town is the one thing it can't out-make. Keep her walking. I'll keep the fire going.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Every cure I brew for scorpion venom stops working a week later. The venom is changing. Put down four of them and I can study this week's batch before it becomes next week's.

Choices.Label: Four scorpions it is.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Mind the tails. I'd rather study venom than drain it out of you.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Then I'll keep guessing. Badly, probably. It's in the journal.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Magic frays near the bad ground -- except the hags'. They bind their workings into their own claws, and it holds. Three claws and I might learn how.

Choices.Label: We'll bring three claws.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: Gloves. Please. I'm serious about the gloves.

Nodes.Speaker: alchemist
Nodes.Text: The fens aren't going anywhere. Unfortunately.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: A ward is only as strong as its weakest stone. I'd like to see whether yours hold. Clear the last of the fens and let no one fall.

Choices.Label: Nobody falls.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: Then mind each other. That is the whole of the working.

Nodes.Speaker: enchantress
Nodes.Text: Patience is a ward too. The test will wait.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Frostmaw's cold gets right into the bunks. Three yeti furs and I could line them before somebody wakes up blue.

Choices.Label: Three furs, then.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: The big shaggy ones. Not the ones with the clubs. Well -- those too, if they insist.

Nodes.Speaker: innkeeper
Nodes.Text: Extra blankets it is. For now.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Those ice maulers carry cores that stay cold in my hottest coals. Break three of them. I want to know what's been growing down here all this time.

Choices.Label: Three maulers.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: Hit them where the frost is thinnest. And come back in one piece -- I'm not reforging you.

Nodes.Speaker: smith
Nodes.Text: They'll still be cold tomorrow. That's rather the point.

Nodes.Speaker: with
Nodes.Text: The ghosts in Veshker -- they're people who stood still and never got to stop. I'd like to lay some of them to rest. Five, at least. It feels like owing someone.

Choices.Label: Let's walk them on.
Not now.

Nodes.Speaker: with
Nodes.Text: Thank you. I'll keep count.

Nodes.Speaker: with
Nodes.Text: Later, then. They've waited this long.
